title: Grant applications for road, sewer and RIM Park upgrades
subtitle: Also covered: fireworks by-law review, traffic and licensing amendments, 2025 University Avenue East update, and a Reep Green Solutions presentation.
overview: Council voted to apply for provincial and federal grants to help pay for major infrastructure and building projects. Staff will apply to two Housing-Enabling funds for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive reconstruction, including a new Laurel Creek sanitary pump station. Council also approved applications to the Green and Inclusive Community Buildings program for greenhouse gas and accessibility retrofits at RIM Park and the Moses Springer Community Centre, with City funding committed only if the grants succeed {{vote:m5}} {{vote:m6}}.

Council directed staff to work with neighbouring municipalities on updates to the Fireworks By-law and report back in April 2025, in response to continuing complaints {{vote:m7}}. It also approved traffic and parking by-law amendments and housekeeping changes to four by-laws covering rental licensing, business licensing, property standards and fences {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m4}}.

Staff said the next step for the City-owned 2025 University Avenue East site is technical evaluation of the submissions received. Staff will then report back to Council with a short list. Council also heard from Reep Green Solutions on its community climate programs. After the public session, Council resumed a closed meeting on labour, land and litigation matters. The minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Staff will apply for up to $6.8 million (water systems) and up to $5.1 million (core servicing) for the Beaver Creek Road and Conservation Drive project, and the Mayor and Clerk may sign agreements if successful.

decisions.item: Green and Inclusive Community Buildings grants
decisions.detail: Council approved applications for the RIM Park retrofit (up to $15,000,000) and Moses Springer Community Centre retrofit ($2,999,999), with $4,000,000 and $600,000 of City funding released only if the grants succeed.
Staff will work with area municipalities on possible Fireworks By-law updates and report back in April 2025.
Council approved report IPPW2024-046 and updated Traffic and Parking By-law #08-077 at various locations.
Council approved amendments to the Residential Rental Licensing, Comprehensive Business Licensing, Property Standards and Fence by-laws.

debate: Asked what happens if the water and servicing grants are not awarded, staff said they would return to Council to discuss advancing the project with City funding alone. Staff noted the project relies heavily on development charges and debt financing, and said cost-sharing with developers could be explored.

On the buildings grants, staff said the program funds 80% from the federal government. If unsuccessful, staff would use the existing capital project reserve and look at other capital programs to leverage funding. One councillor said reliance on grants shows the need for a municipal fiscal review.

On fireworks, a councillor noted rising complaints despite earlier changes to times, days and locations and a shift to drone and light shows. The councillor argued for a regional approach and a coordinated communication strategy. Staff said cross-divisional research on other municipalities' regulation is under way, and the regional work would include a communications plan.

On 2025 University Avenue East, staff said the City is targeting at least 700 affordable units there. Staff said submissions will be checked against City goals, servicing capacity, transportation and open space before a short list goes to Council.
